records.event: Anzu Robotics, Cogito Tech / SPECTA, and SkyRover / Knowact exhibit significant gray zone risks due to their reliance on DJI hardware, firmware, and cloud infrastructure, as well as manufacturing and component sourcing from adversary nations.
records.evidence_basis: Teardown analysis confirms identical PCB layouts and components with DJI Mavic 3 and Air 3 for Anzu Robotics and Cogito Tech/SPECTA, respectively. Firmware for Anzu Robotics is signed with DJI cryptographic keys and built on DJI SDK, while SkyRover/Knowact apps connect directly to DJI cloud infrastructure and use identical encryption keys. All three entities, along with Autel Robotics, are identified with manufacturing and/or data hosting in adversary nations and high percentages of components sourced from adversary nations.
records.impact: Increased regulatory scrutiny and potential inclusion on restricted lists for these entities, impacting their market access and operational viability in the US and allied nations. This also highlights a broader supply chain vulnerability for UAS technology.
records.region: Global, specifically US and allied nations
records.comparison_basis: same question and criteria; shared evidence

records.event: The U.S. Marine Corps will continue to prioritize the acquisition and integration of electronic warfare jammers to protect Amphibious Combat Vehicles (ACVs) from drone threats.
records.evidence_basis: The U.S. Marine Corps is buying Anduril Pulsar-L electronic warfare jammers to meet an urgent operational need to better protect its 8x8 wheeled Amphibious Combat Vehicles (ACV) from drones. This is part of broader efforts the service is pursuing to boost the ACV’s defenses against uncrewed aerial attackers, as well as incoming anti-tank guided missiles and other threats. Drone threats are real now and have notably sidelined even the most advanced he.
records.impact: Increased demand for electronic warfare systems and counter-UAS capabilities for ground vehicles within the USMC, potentially influencing future procurement cycles and R&D investments.
drivers: Urgent operational need to protect ACVs from drone threats
Observed effectiveness of drones in modern warfare
records.comparison_basis: same question and criteria; shared evidence

records.event: The U.S. Navy's new Robotic and Autonomous Systems Warfighting Development Center (RASWDC) will accelerate the integration of drones, unmanned boats, and robotic submarines into naval combat operations.
records.evidence_basis: The U.S. Navy has set up a new command to turn its growing collection of drones, unmanned boats and robotic submarines into tools sailors can actually fight with, naming Rear Adm. Melvin Smith as its first commander. The Robotic and Autonomous Systems Warfighting Development Center, known as RASWDC, is headquartered at Joint Expeditionary Base Little.
records.impact: Increased demand for autonomous systems and related technologies (AI, C2, sensors) within the U.S. Navy, potentially leading to new acquisition programs and R&D investments in unmanned warfare capabilities.
drivers: U.S. Navy's strategic focus on drone warfare
Need to effectively integrate existing and future unmanned assets into combat

records.event: The U.S. Air Force's contract with DZYNE Technologies for the ULTRA glider-like surveillance drone will see further value increases or follow-on contracts for expanded operational testing or procurement.
records.evidence_basis: The U.S. Air Force has more than doubled the value of its contract with DZYNE Technologies for operational testing of ULTRA, a glider-like surveillance drone that can stay in the air for more than three days, the U.S. Department of War announced. The $46.1 million modification raises the contract’s total value to $85.6 million, up.
assumptions: The ULTRA drone continues to perform successfully in operational testing.
The U.S. Air Force identifies a sustained need for long-endurance surveillance capabilities.
alternatives: Testing may reveal limitations, leading to a reduction or termination of the program.
Alternative surveillance drone technologies may emerge that are more cost-effective or performant.
change_indicators: Further contract modifications or announcements regarding ULTRA drone procurement or deployment.
Public statements from USAF officials regarding the success or expansion of the ULTRA program.
records.impact: Increased market opportunity for DZYNE Technologies and other companies specializing in long-endurance, glider-based UAS. Could indicate a shift in USAF surveillance strategy towards more persistent, less detectable platforms.
drivers: Demonstrated capability of ULTRA for extended surveillance (more than three days)
USAF's investment in expanding operational testing
